title: Backend performance review — finding
description: One finding from a backend performance review. Mirrors the finding format in SKILL.md; the Markdown report remains the primary human artifact and this is the machine-readable form of the same content. Priority must match the matrix published in SKILL.md — that cross-field rule is enforced by scripts/check_repo_invariants.py against the matrix as published, so the matrix is not duplicated here.

id.description: Report-local identifier. Not stable across reviews — see stable_id.

stable_id.description: Identity that survives line-number changes, refactoring, and file moves. Derived from root cause, file, enclosing symbol, and mechanism — never from a line number. Two reviews of the same unfixed problem must produce the same stable_id; this is what makes historical comparison, fix verification, and run-to-run stability measurable.

root_cause_id.description: Findings that are symptoms of one underlying constraint share a root_cause_id. Merging is mandatory (methodology/bottleneck-analysis.md §2); this field is how a merge is recorded rather than merely performed.

state.description: Lifecycle state. A first review emits OPEN for everything; later states arrive from re-review or from the consuming team.

severity.description: Impact if real. Derived from the four factors in `impact`, per SKILL.md §Severity.

confidence.description: An evidence grade — how sure you are this is real, not how much it matters. `Confirmed` requires a cited runtime artifact; uncited Confirmed is a violation.

priority.description: Derived from the severity/confidence matrix in SKILL.md. Never chosen directly, and never influenced by how cheap the fix is.

category.description: Kept in exact agreement with the Category enum in SKILL.md; check_repo_invariants.py enforces both directions.

service.description: Which service this belongs to, for a monorepo. Matches a name in the review envelope's services[].

symbol.description: Enclosing function, method, or class. Part of stable_id, and more durable than a line number.

performance_principle.description: The universal principle violated, stated without reference to the technology. Reasoning that starts at the technology produces advice that is true in general and useless here.

evidence.description: What in the repository or in supplied runtime artifacts supports this. Every entry carries its provenance, so a reader can tell a line of code from a production trace.

evidence_quality.description: How good the evidence is, as distinct from how sure the conclusion is. A production trace is Strong; a plausible reading of one file is Weak. Confidence may not exceed what evidence quality supports.

impact.description: The four severity factors, made explicit rather than summarized. SKILL.md requires all four for every finding.

growth.description: Growth in data or traffic. `unknown` is a legitimate answer and is preferred over an invented complexity — derive it only where the code supports the derivation.

amplification.description: Work multiplier from fan-out, retries, N+1, pagination loops, or cache misses. A numeric factor only where it is derivable from the code; otherwise `Nx` or `unknown`. Never estimated.

conditions.description: The workload under which this matters. May never be empty — a finding that cannot state its conditions does not ship. Where workload is unknown, the assumption is stated here and confidence caps at Medium.

counter_evidence.description: Evidence sought against this finding, not for it. Required, and an empty array is a positive assertion that a search was made and nothing was found — not that none was attempted. Anything found here must be reflected in `confidence`.

why_this_might_not_matter.description: The strongest honest case that this finding is not worth acting on. Required at Medium severity and above, where the cost of a false positive is highest.

recommendation.description: What to change, and why it addresses the principle rather than the symptom.

alternatives.description: Options considered, with the preferred one named and justified. Guards against the failure where the first plausible fix is the only one examined — usually the one that masks work rather than removing it.

trade_offs.description: Complexity, memory, consistency, operational burden, new failure modes. A recommendation that states no cost has not been thought through.

validation.description: How to prove the change worked, structured so it can be checked mechanically rather than only read.

kind.description: static: read from the repository. runtime: a measurement artifact. user-provided: stated by the user. derived: computed from other evidence, with its inputs shown in `statement`.

tool.description: For runtime evidence, what produced it — EXPLAIN, a profiler, a load test, a trace exporter.

timestamp.description: When the runtime artifact was captured. A six-month-old trace is weaker evidence than a fresh one, and the reader cannot tell without this.

effect.description: What this did to the finding. `lowers-confidence` and `bounds-impact` must be visible in the scores above; `refutes` means the candidate should not have become a finding at all.

why.description: Required on the preferred option — why this one rather than the others.

metric.description: What to measure. Specific enough to act on: "query count on GET /orders", not "performance".

baseline.description: The current value, only where it was actually measured. Omit rather than estimate — an invented baseline is a fabricated number.

expectation.description: A prediction, not a promise. Direction of change is always assertable; magnitude only where derivable from the code.

falsifier.description: What observation would mean this finding was wrong. If no observation could refute it, it is not an engineering claim.

guard.description: A test, metric, or alert that stops the problem recurring once fixed.
